headline: Investigation report filed against 11, including Sheikh Hasina, in Ekramul 'crossfire' murder
summary: The prosecution has filed a formal complaint against 11 individuals, including Sheikh Hasina, at the International Crimes Tribunal-2 regarding the 2018 'crossfire' killing of Commissioner Ekramul Haque in Cox's Bazar.
details: The prosecution has filed a formal complaint against 11 individuals, including Sheikh Hasina, at the International Crimes Tribunal-2. This complaint concerns the 2018 'crossfire' killing of Commissioner Ekramul Haque in Cox's Bazar. The filing took place on Sunday, July 26, before Tribunal-2, led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury.

In a separate development at the same tribunal, the prosecution also submitted a formal complaint against 19 individuals, including former MP Saiful Islam. This relates to the killing of Ashabul Yamin during the July mass uprising in Savar.

Furthermore, journalist Ashraf Kausar is scheduled to testify today as the 27th witness in another ongoing case. This case involves seven individuals, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader, regarding allegations of killings, conspiracy, and incitement during the July mass uprising.

headline: Govt to place draft law on enforced disappearances at next cabinet meeting
summary: Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman announced draft laws on preventing enforced disappearances and reforming the National Human Rights Commission are in final stages. These will be presented at the next cabinet meeting.
details: Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman announced yesterday that draft laws on preventing enforced disappearances and reforming the National Human Rights Commission will be placed before the next cabinet meeting. If approved by the cabinet, these crucial bills would then proceed to parliament for further deliberation.

The minister confirmed that the draft laws are in their final stages, following extensive consultations with civil society, heads of disciplined forces, and other stakeholders. The government also invited written feedback via email to ensure comprehensive input.

Former Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury, who headed the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, highlighted the severe psychological impact on survivors. He noted that many victims suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder and serious mental trauma, requiring urgent medical treatment and formal rehabilitation.

Maroof Zaman, a former ambassador and survivor of enforced disappearance, expressed frustration over the slow pace of legal proceedings for victims. Tajul Islam, former chief prosecutor, stressed that criminal prosecution must be the primary step for justice before discussing truth and reconciliation.
caption:
Bangladesh's government is set to introduce draft laws addressing enforced disappearances and human rights commission reforms. This move aims to improve justice access for victims.

Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman announced yesterday that draft laws on preventing enforced disappearances and reforming the National Human Rights Commission will be placed before the next cabinet meeting. If approved by the cabinet, these crucial bills would then proceed to parliament for further deliberation.

The minister confirmed that the draft laws are in their final stages, following extensive consultations with civil society, heads of disciplined forces, and other stakeholders. The government also invited written feedback via email to ensure comprehensive input.

Former Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury, who headed the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, highlighted the severe psychological impact on survivors. He noted that many victims suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder and serious mental trauma, requiring urgent medical treatment and formal rehabilitation.

Maroof Zaman, a former ambassador and survivor of enforced disappearance, expressed frustration over the slow pace of legal proceedings for victims. Tajul Islam, former chief prosecutor, stressed that criminal prosecution must be the primary step for justice before discussing truth and reconciliation.
